diagnostic_evidence.quote: While our architecture inherently ensures symplecticity, exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced
with relative errors on the order of machine precision

issues.failure_explanation: Symplecticity of the learned maps does not imply that H is conserved. The paper itself says conservation is not enforced and is only encouraged by a soft penalty with weight λ2. The introduction still claims energy conservation is ensured. Example 3 reports machine-precision Hamiltonian errors for a learned surrogate with reconstruction MSE of about 1e-7, which is incompatible with the stated lack of exact conservation unless the plotted quantity is the reference integrator's. No argument is given.

failure_location.quote: ensuring energy conservation and numerical stability through nonlinear transformations

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that only the symplectic structure is guaranteed and that H is conserved only approximately, through the penalty. Reword the Example 3 claim to say what the plotted quantity is.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee advertised for the ROM (energy conservation, and exact Hamiltonian preservation in the conclusion) is not established by the architecture. The numerical conservation evidence is only empirical.
issues.title: Symplecticity is claimed to ensure energy conservation, contradicting the paper's own statement
issues.why_classification: Rewording the claim removes the defect; no method, theorem or experiment needs to change.

issues.failure_explanation: For H(V,η)(x,y) = (y+η, x+∇V(y)) the Jacobian is M = [[0,I],[I,H_V]], and a direct computation gives M^T J M = −J. So the single Hénon map is anti-symplectic, not symplectic. Only even powers, such as the fourth-power layer, are symplectic. The embedding in Section 3.2 uses the opposite sign (−Px), as in the original Hénon construction, so the two definitions are inconsistent. The inverse formula in the proposition matches the +x convention and would change under the −x sign.

failure_location.quote: The fundamental building block is the H\'enon mapping, which enables intricate nonlinear transformations while preserving symplectic structure:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the −x convention consistently (and correct the inverse formula), or state that each map is anti-symplectic and that the fourth-power layer is symplectic.
issues.overall_effect: The statement about the elementary building block is false. The layer-level symplecticity claim survives only because of the fourth power, and the paper never says so. The embedding and the HénonNet use inconsistent conventions.
issues.title: Hénon map as defined is anti-symplectic, and its sign is inconsistent with the embedding map
issues.why_classification: A local sign or wording fix restores consistency, and the layer-level symplecticity claim holds either way.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: More critically, H\'enonNet has been proven to possess a universal approximation theorem for nonlinear symplectic mappings~\cite{turaev2002polynomial}

issues.failure_explanation: No proof is given. The cited universality concerns symplectic diffeomorphisms of R^{2n}, while σ = H∘G∘ι only approximates Φ through a global symplectic diffeomorphism restricted to ι(Ω). Extending an arbitrary embedding to such a diffeomorphism is a nontrivial step, and it can fail. Take k=n, Ω an annulus, and Φ an area-preserving radial map onto an annulus whose inner circle encloses area 9π instead of π. Any homeomorphism σ that is C^0-close to Φ must map the disc bounded by the inner circle onto a region of area at least about 9π, which contradicts area preservation, so the theorem is false there. The statement also quantifies over 'parameters of ι', although ι is fixed and not learned. The Section 3.2 claim that a fixed ι 'suffices' relies on the same unproven step.

failure_location.quote: Let $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{2k}\to \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be an arbitrary symplectic embedding defined on a compact domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{2k}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to embeddings that extend to symplectic diffeomorphisms of R^{2n}, or to contractible Ω with k<n plus a proved extension lemma. Then apply the cited diffeomorphism-level universality to the extension, and drop 'parameters of ι'.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed theoretical guarantee for the composite embedding, and the justification for using a fixed canonical ι without losing accuracy, are unsupported as stated and false in the generality claimed.
issues.title: Universal approximation of arbitrary symplectic embeddings is stated without proof and does not follow from the cited diffeomorphism result
issues.why_classification: A restricted hypothesis plus an extension argument gives a comparable theorem; the method is unaffected, but the stated generality is lost and a nontrivial lemma is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we investigate symplectic reduced-order modeling (ROM) for parametric Hamiltonian systems

issues.failure_explanation: The encoder and the flow map y_{i+1}=f_flow(y_i) take no parameter input. In Examples 2 and 3 the initial state does not depend on the parameter (κ(ω), respectively ε), so every parameter gives the same latent initial state y_0. An autonomous, parameter-free map then produces the same latent trajectory, and the same decoded prediction, for all parameters, although the true dynamics differ (different wave speeds, different ε). The loss L_f with conflicting targets from the same y_0 cannot be driven to zero. The claimed accurate parametric predictions from the initial condition are therefore not supported by the stated architecture.

failure_location.quote: approximated by an autonomous, discrete-time symplectic flow map

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Make the encoder or flow-map HénonNet parameter-conditioned, for example V_i(y;μ) and η_i(μ). This keeps symplecticity for each fixed μ. Then rerun the parametric experiments, or restrict the claims to non-parametric settings.
issues.overall_effect: The framing as a ROM for parametric systems, and the parametric extrapolation results in Examples 2 and 3, are not supported by the architecture as specified.
issues.title: Parameter-free latent flow cannot represent the parameter-dependent dynamics claimed in the parametric examples
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained architectural change plus re-training, but it adds a new construction and invalidates the existing parametric results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a formally complete parametrization, $4n$ G-reflector layers are needed.

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own criterion, completeness needs 4n reflectors, which is 800 or more here since n=N=200 in Examples 1 and 2 and 256 in Example 3. The experiments use 100 layers for the linear baseline and 10 in the composite. A finite-width, finite-depth HénonNet is also only a universal approximator, not a complete parameterization of the nonlinear manifold. The reported comparisons therefore do not compare complete parameterizations, and the claim that more linear layers give limited improvement is not tested.

failure_location.quote: whereas the others offer complete parameterizations of the corresponding linear or non-linear symplectic embedding manifolds

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State that the tested G-reflector models are truncated, with 10 or 100 layers instead of 4n, and describe HénonNet only as an approximator. Alternatively, add experiments with the full number of reflectors.
issues.overall_effect: The 'complete vs incomplete parameterization' framing used to interpret the MSE tables is not what was tested. The G-reflector baseline is a truncated parameterization.
issues.title: Claim of complete parameterizations contradicts the 4n-reflector requirement and the layer counts actually used
issues.why_classification: Rewording the scope of the claim suffices; the reported numbers and the method are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Training data use a_0 in [7,8], the problem statement allows [7,9], and the showcased case has a_0 = 8.939, which is outside the training range. Either the sampling range is misreported or the showcased prediction is an unacknowledged parameter extrapolation. The text cites only time extrapolation as evidence of robustness, so the demonstrated performance cannot be attributed to what was claimed.

failure_location.quote: We generate snapshot data by uniformly sampling 3000 parameter pairs $(a_0,x_0)$ from $[7,8]\times[-0.2,0.2]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the training range to [7,9] if that was used, or show the figure for an in-range parameter and say explicitly that extrapolation is being tested.
issues.overall_effect: The representative result for Example 1 cannot be interpreted as in-distribution accuracy, and the description of the experiment is inconsistent.
issues.title: Example 1 test parameter lies outside the stated training parameter range
issues.why_classification: It is a local correction of the experimental description or of the displayed case.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notably, despite training only on data up to $t = 12$, the model successfully extrapolates to $t = 24$

issues.failure_explanation: The formula u(x,t)=u^0(x−ωt) is the whole-line travelling wave. With u^0 supported in nearly all of [0,1] and ω=0.1, the shifted profile violates u(1,t)=0 almost immediately, since the support at t=0 can reach x=0.986 and moves right. By t=24 the shift is 2.4, so reflections at the Dirichlet walls dominate. The equation reference also points to the spline definition rather than the PDE. The reference data are in fact numerical Störmer–Verlet solutions, so the closed-form 'exact' solution is wrong for the stated problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the closed form, or state the solution as the method-of-images solution with reflections, or restrict it to times before the pulse reaches the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The stated closed-form solution cannot be used for validation or interpretation beyond the earliest times.
issues.title: Stated 'exact solution' of the Dirichlet wave problem does not satisfy the boundary conditions
issues.why_classification: It is a local factual correction that does not touch the method or the reported numerics.

issues.failure_explanation: With z=(q,p) and J=[[0,I],[−I,0]], the stated model q_t=p, p_t=ω²D_xx q requires ∇H = Lz with L=diag(−ω²D_xx, I). The paper's L=diag(I, ω²D_xx) instead gives q̇=ω²D_xx p and ṗ=−q, which is not the wave equation. In Example 2, L uses ω² although the wave speed is κ(ω) and ω is a 4-vector, so ω² is undefined. This is inconsistent with the Hamiltonian given in the same example.

failure_location.quote: \bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L \, \mathbf{z}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L by diag(−κ D_xx, I), with κ=ω² in Example 1, and fix the Δx scaling of the gradient.
issues.overall_effect: The stated discrete systems do not generate the stated dynamics, so the reference-data generation is mis-specified on paper.
issues.title: Wave-equation semi-discretization: L has blocks swapped and a sign error, and uses ω² instead of κ(ω)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the formulas, which are forced by the stated PDE and Hamiltonian.

issues.failure_explanation: q_t=p_xx+ε|u|²p and p_t=−q_xx−ε|u|²q correspond to H=∫−½(q_x²+p_x²)+(ε/4)(q²+p²)², not to the stated H_cont. With H_cont as written, q_t=∂H/∂p=−2p_xx+2ε|u|²p, which flips the sign of the dispersion relative to the nonlinearity (defocusing instead of focusing) and carries different constants. The discrete H has a quadratic, not quartic, nonlinear term ε/4(p²+q²), so its gradient is linear. Its difference term q_i²(q_{i−1}−q_i)² is also not a gradient energy. Its gradient therefore cannot equal Lz+g(z). Moreover g(z) contains no ε, so the discrete flow does not depend on the parameter ε at all.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive H from the ODE: H=Δx Σ[−½((q_{i+1}−q_i)²+(p_{i+1}−p_i)²)/Δx² + (ε/4)(q_i²+p_i²)²]. Include ε in g, and re-verify that the experiments used these formulas.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamiltonian used in L_ham for Example 3 and in the conservation diagnostic is not an invariant of the stated dynamics. The parametric dependence on ε is lost in the discretization as written.
issues.title: Schrödinger Hamiltonians (continuous and discrete) are inconsistent with the equations of motion, and ε is dropped from g
issues.why_classification: The repair is a formula correction forced by the ODE, but it affects the training loss and conservation evidence and so needs verification or rerun of Example 3.
